text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides reveals his intention to run for a top position in right-wing Disy in party elections, while another MP lambasts ministers for undermining its chairman, Yiannakis Matsis.
- Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou hits back at budget critics during parliamentary debate.
- The United States and the European Union have agreed to coordinate efforts to promote progress on the Cyprus problem.
- Tourism chiefs ask for more hospitality, less talk of war.
- "No miracles" are expected from U.K. tourism, leading travel experts have suggested.
- Cyprus is poised to sign the WTO global telecom pact.
- Political parties debate the 1997 state budget. Socialist Edek is opposed.
- France expresses its willingness to participate with its own contingent in a multinational force in Cyprus.
- Communist Akel tables a debate on the freedom of the media to parliament.
- Trade unions disagree between themselves over President Glafcos Clerides's proposal on cost of living allowances.
- Families in the Ayios Dhometios area of Nicosia live under the permanent threat posed by Turkish soldiers.
